questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Which country works the longest hours
How to decorate a home office
Why people prefer working in offices
Flexible working and the right to ask for it
questions.why: They discuss what flexible working means and the UK right to request it.

questions.q: How long have UK employees had the right to request flexible working?
options: For the last 14 years
Only since the pandemic
For the last 4 years
For over 40 years
questions.why: Georgina says for the last 14 years employees have had the right to request flexible working.

questions.q: According to Sarah Jackson, what does flexible working really mean?
options: Always working from home
Working fewer hours for the same pay
Choosing when, where and how long you work
Choosing your own manager
questions.why: She says it means choice and control over when, where and how long you work, agreed with your manager.

questions.q: Which request does Neil give as a sensible example?
options: Working only two hours a day from home
Working from 12 until 8 instead of 9 to 5
Never going into the office again at all
Taking every Friday off to see your family
questions.why: Neil says working two hours a day isn't sensible, but 12 until 8 instead of 9 to 5 might be.

questions.q: Who was the law first for?
options: Everyone who worked in an office
Only men with young children at home
Workers over the age of 60
Parents of young or disabled children
questions.why: Neil says it was initially just for parents with a child under 6 or a disabled child under 18.

questions.q: What problem does Sarah Jackson describe for men?
options: They never ask for flexible working
Their requests are more likely to be rejected
They don't want to spend time with children
They are paid less when they work flexibly
questions.why: She says men, when they do ask, are more likely to be turned down.

questions.q: What does Sarah Jackson want employers to do?
options: Encourage men to ask for it
Stop all flexible working immediately
Give flexible working only to women
Pay fathers to stay at home
questions.why: She says employers should say to men, 'please use the right to request flexible working'.

questions.q: Why does Sarah Jackson think this is so important?
options: It will make companies more profitable
It will reduce traffic in busy cities
It's needed for equality at home and work
Young men want to work longer hours
questions.why: She says until men can be active fathers, we won't get equality at home or in the workplace.
